---
title: "Sparse Attention"
description: "An attention pattern that limits which positions can interact, reducing computation or encoding useful structure."
term: "Sparse Attention"
letter: "S"
category: "LLM Engineering"
difficulty: "Advanced"
---

## Simple explanation

Full attention lets every token attend to every other allowed token.
Sparse attention restricts those connections, for example to nearby tokens
or selected global positions, to make long sequences more manageable.

## Technical explanation

Sparse attention computes attention over a subset or structured pattern of
query-key pairs rather than a dense matrix. Patterns include local windows,
strided connections, block sparsity, and selected global tokens. The
theoretical reduction in work depends on sequence length and pattern, while
practical speed depends on kernels and hardware.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Attention memory and computation can grow quadratically with sequence
length in dense implementations. Sparse patterns can extend usable context
or reduce cost, but may limit information flow and complicate parallel
execution.

## How it works

The model applies a mask or sparse kernel so each query computes attention
only over permitted keys. The pattern may be fixed, learned, or based on
content. Engineers must verify that the implementation actually exploits
sparsity rather than merely masking a dense calculation.

## Practical example

A long-document model can use local attention for nearby tokens and add
selected global tokens for document-wide information. Compare quality and
end-to-end latency with a dense baseline on the target sequence lengths.

## Common misconceptions

- A sparse mask alone does not guarantee faster computation if the runtime
  still materializes dense attention.
- Sparsity changes which information can interact; it is an architectural
  choice, not only an implementation optimization.
